layer1.name: RouteLedger
layer1.one_liner: Delivery route reconciliation for regional courier firms.
layer1.description: Reconciles driver-reported stops against dispatch records. Included because its synthesiser was unusually talkative: the ledger carries far more model inference than sourced evidence.
layer1.outcome_note: Synthetic fixture. Not a real company and not counted toward separation statistics.

layer2.pins: The model_inference swing clamp, end to end through the runner rather than in a unit test. Twelve high-confidence inference claims sit against two sourced ones. The support value must land within 8 points of what the two sourced claims produce alone — if a future change lets the synthesiser's own opinions accumulate, this entry's score moves and the hard rule in PRD 5.3 has quietly stopped being a cap.

assumptions.statement: At least 5 in 10 regional courier firms running 20 or more vehicles have written off more than $2000 in unreconciled stops in the past quarter

falsification_criterion.applies_to: regional courier firms running 20 or more vehicles
falsification_criterion.observation: ask the operations lead to pull last quarter's unreconciled stop total

claims.text: An operations manager describes writing off unreconciled stops every quarter.
claims.retrieved_text: Synthetic fixture text. Not retrieved from any real source.

claims.text: A trade publication describes reconciliation as a persistent margin leak in regional courier work.
claims.retrieved_text: Synthetic fixture text. Not retrieved from any real source.

claims.text: No evidence found either way on write-off size for firms under 50 vehicles.
Reconciliation gaps are plausibly larger where dispatch and driver systems are separate.
Manual stop reconciliation is likely to scale poorly with fleet size.
Quarterly close is a plausible point at which the loss becomes visible.
Firms without dedicated operations staff plausibly absorb the loss silently.
The write-off threshold is plausibly lower for firms on fixed-price contracts.
Driver-reported data is likely to diverge from dispatch records over time.
Seasonal peaks plausibly widen the reconciliation gap.
Paper proof-of-delivery is plausibly correlated with larger gaps.
Larger fleets plausibly have more tooling and smaller relative losses.
The problem is plausibly worse in firms with high driver turnover.
Subcontracted routes plausibly reconcile worse than owned ones.
